invariants.name: A pass has each skill and the total at or under their caps
A fail names a skill or a total over its cap
The lower step never raises a cap

carrier.contract: The gate maps the word counts of the skill trees and one budget to one report. A count over its cap is a problem that names the skill, and a count under its cap is a note.

category.equality: Two reports are equal when their problem lists and their note lists are equal in order. Two budgets are equal when their total caps and their skill caps are equal.

laws.reason: The gate runs three arrows side by side from one main function, and the record declares no composite arrow. This change adds no composition operator, map, functor or monad.

abstraction.hides: The walk of each skill tree, the word split of each Markdown file and the format of the cap file.
callersKnow: A skill or the total over its cap fails the gate, and the failure names it.
A skill with no cap fails the gate.
A cap above its count passes with a note, and the lower step sets it to the count.
A cap rises only in a PR that moves text into that skill while the total falls by more, and review enforces that rule.
abstraction.deletionTest: Deleting budgetReport puts the cap comparison and the problem text in main and in each test. Deleting lowerBudget makes each cut PR edit the cap file by hand.

alternatives.name: A lint warning for skill size
alternatives.rejectedBecause: A warning does not stop growth.

alternatives.name: A total cap only
alternatives.rejectedBecause: One skill can then grow while another shrinks.

alternatives.name: Fail a cap above its count
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Each commit of a cut PR then needs a cap edit.

omitted: The notes of the report and the cap of a gone skill have no model state. The unit tests examine them.
The model takes the word count of each skill tree as a true observation.
The duplicate map and its cut rule are outside the model. The wb-successor control examines each cut name from mattpocock/skills and with no lock entry.

bounds: Two skills, counts from 0 to 2, a start cap of 1 for each skill and a start total cap of 2.
Each order of the edit, check and lower steps.

negative.defect: A gate that reads only the total passes a skill over its cap while the total stays under its cap.

limits: The finite model takes the word counts as true observations and covers two skills only.
The model does not show that the TypeScript code refines it. The linked controls and review examine that relation.
The rule that a cap rises only while the total falls by more has no check, because the gate cannot see a PR. The PR body gives the rise of 1,152 words and the fall of 4,288 words.
The model does not check the words of the moved rules, the routes or the ADR notes. Review, validate and the STE gates examine them.
Exact-head CI, review, Shipping and every ordinary gate stay required.
